claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 9 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 9 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the age of the child you're claiming for:**

Do you have:
- **A child under 16 years old**, OR
- **A young person aged 16-19 years old**, OR
- **A child aged 20 or over**?

Please tell me the age (or age range) of the child(ren) you're inquiring about, and I'll guide you through the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex is 9 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 9 years old, so he falls into the under 16 category, which means he's a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

Let me continue with the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:**

Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?

(This is a standard check - children under 16 who are working full-time or receiving certain benefits may not qualify)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 9, so he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's clear - Alex is in primary school and not working, so he definitely qualifies on that front.

Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about benefits:**

Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

In other words, is Alex not receiving any of these state benefits independently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right, which is what we need.

Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about apprenticeships:**

Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?

Since he's only 9 years old and in primary school, I'd expect the answer is no - but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's only 9 and still in primary school, so no apprenticeships or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Alex is clearly not in any apprenticeship, which is good.

Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to ask about your residency situation:**

This is an important check. To qualify for Child Benefit, you need to meet UK residency requirements. Let me ask:

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - this is the most common situation
2. You have **settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. You have **pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** and are:
   - Working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - Actively seeking work, OR
   - Have sufficient resources and aren't claiming Income Support/JSA/Pension Credit/Universal Credit, OR
   - Studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - A family member of an EEA or Swiss national
4. You're a **Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which of these situations applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - we live in Manchester. I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that, just a regular resident here.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! You normally live in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirements. That's straightforward.

Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex:**

To claim Child Benefit, you must be responsible for the child. This means one of the following:

1. **You live with the child** - you share a home with Alex
2. **You contribute to their upkeep** - you pay for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc., at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount
3. **You pay maintenance under court order or agreement** - formal maintenance payments that cover their upkeep

Which of these applies to you and Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me - we share the same house in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You live with Alex, so you definitely meet the responsibility requirement.

Let me continue to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about other claimants:**

Is there anyone else (such as the other parent, grandparent, or other family member) who is currently claiming or might also claim Child Benefit for Alex?

Or have you and any other potential claimant already agreed on who should claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one who would be claiming for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good, so you're the only potential claimant for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to ask about Alex's living situation:**

Is Alex:
- **In hospital** currently, OR
- **In care** (residential care facility), OR
- **Fostered**, OR
- **Living normally at home with you** (the typical situation)

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is just living normally at home with me - nothing special like hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final eligibility question:**

Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance (housing, food, etc.)?

In other words, you're fully funding Alex's care yourself without council support?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - I pay for everything myself. The council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final piece of information I need. Based on all the answers you've provided, I can now give you your eligibility result.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me report your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

### Summary:
**Congratulations!** You meet all the eligibility criteria to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

### What this means:
- You can claim Child Benefit for Alex (age 9)
- Alex meets all qualifying requirements
- You have demonstrated responsibility for him
- Your residency and financial arrangements all comply with the rules

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

You now need to **apply for Child Benefit**. Here's what to do:

1. **Apply online** at gov.uk/apply-child-benefit, or
2. **Apply by post** using form CH2 (available from the UK government website)

### What you'll need to provide:
- Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
- Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
- Proof of your UK residency

### Important note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:
If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the **High Income Child Benefit Charge**. This means you'd need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through Self Assessment. Even if this applies, it's still worth claiming.

### Payment Details:
- Child Benefit is paid **every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)
- You'll receive it directly into your bank account

**Good luck with your application!** For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
